title: A Parish for the Letter
premise: August Iversen, a concierge at the Hotel Verlaine who prides herself on noticing what others miss, is hired to find Marguerite Voss, a translator who vanished from room 412. The case turns strange when August discovers Marguerite's diary in the hotel's lost-and-found, its entries continuing for weeks after her disappearance — including one describing August herself, written in handwriting that matches her own. Following the diary's clues, August uncovers a decades-old cover-up: Marguerite witnessed a fatal hit-and-run by a beloved local judge, and the 'dead' witness everyone swears is gone has been living hidden inside the hotel under an assumed identity, protected by staff who chose justice outside the law. In the climax, August confronts the judge in the hotel's sealed fourth floor, where Marguerite has been hiding in plain sight as the night porter; the diary's final entry, written by Marguerite in imitation of August as a message only she would understand, leads to the confession that frees them both.
about_author: Freya Joubert spent nine years working night desks in grand European hotels before turning to fiction, collecting the small dramas of lobbies and luggage carts along the way. She writes mysteries about people who watch for a living, and lives above a bookshop with an unreasonably opinionated cat.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Checked Out Sideways
chapters.summary: August Iversen's POV. A routine morning at the Hotel Verlaine breaks when lawyer Edvard Lund hires August to find Marguerite Voss, missing eleven days from room 412. August's pride in closing every case meets her first unease: the room was cleaned, but the Bible is upside down. Beat: confident competence shadowed by the first wrong note.

chapters.title: Room 412, Twice Cleaned
chapters.summary: August searches the room against protocol, finding a pressed violet in the mattress seam and scratch marks inside the wardrobe. Housekeeper Sanna claims nothing was there; her hands shake. POV August. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling into the sense that the hotel itself is lying to her.

chapters.title: Lost and Found
chapters.summary: In the basement archive, August finds Marguerite's diary logged as abandoned luggage. Its last dated entry is three days before the disappearance — but later pages continue past it, describing the hotel after she vanished. POV August. Beat: vertigo; the object that should end the case instead opens a door.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: August reads the impossible entries through the night: Marguerite writing about a funeral she supposedly attended, a man called 'the Judge,' and a warning addressed to 'whoever finds this.' POV August, with diary excerpts. Beat: obsession taking root; sleep becomes optional.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Buried
chapters.summary: August traces the diary's references to a 1998 hit-and-run on Fjordgaten: a cyclist killed, a witness who recanted then disappeared, presiding over the settlement — Judge Halvard Rye, the city's beloved philanthropist. POV August. Beat: the case stops being a missing person and becomes something older and colder.

chapters.title: What Sanna Knows
chapters.summary: August corners housekeeper Sanna, who nearly quits rather than talk, then whispers that some guests 'stay without staying.' She begs August to stop before the day manager hears. POV Sanna briefly, then August. Beat: first ally, first threat; loyalty inside the hotel runs deeper than law.

chapters.title: The Man Who Isn't on the Roster
chapters.summary: August audits staff records and finds a night porter, Tomas Lindqvist, employed since 2001 but absent from every photograph, payroll anomaly, and memory except the oldest employees'. POV August. Beat: the hotel's blind spots have a shape, and it walks the corridors at night.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: August works a covert overnight, watching Tomas move through the building like water finding cracks. He leaves a violet on the fourth-floor landing. When she approaches, he says only: 'You read it too fast.' POV August. Beat: hunter and hunted exchange places.

chapters.title: Handwriting
chapters.summary: A forensic graphologist confirms the post-disappearance diary entries match August's own hand — not forged, but imitated with uncanny precision, as if written by someone who studied her for years. POV August. Beat: identity destabilized; the case now points inward.

chapters.title: Edvard Lund's Second Client
chapters.summary: August confronts Lund, discovering he once represented the dead cyclist's family and lost everything to Judge Rye. He hired August knowing more than he said — hoping the diary would surface. POV Lund, then August. Beat: grief weaponized into patience; motives blur.

chapters.title: The Fourth Floor
chapters.summary: The hotel's fourth floor is officially closed for renovation, but August finds fresh footprints, a cot, books in translation, and twenty years of newspaper clippings about Judge Rye pinned behind wallpaper. POV August. Beat: awe and dread — someone has been living inside the wound.

chapters.title: Marguerite's First Life
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Marguerite's voice via recovered letters: how she translated for the court in 1998, saw the Judge's car strike the cyclist, recanted under threat, and spent decades drowning in the lie. Beat: sympathy established; the victim becomes a person.

chapters.title: The Judge Comes to Stay
chapters.summary: Judge Halvard Rye checks into the Verlaine for a retirement gala honoring him. August watches him charm the lobby while recognizing his name from the diary margins. POV August. Beat: the predator enters the trap's geography, smiling.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Years of Violets
chapters.summary: Sanna finally confesses: the old staff hid Marguerite in the hotel after she fled Rye's threats, rotating her between identities — porter, archivist, ghost. They chose mercy over testimony because the courts had already failed once. POV Sanna. Beat: the moral heart of the book; justice outside the law given a face.

chapters.title: A Case I Can't Close
chapters.summary: August faces her crisis: exposing Marguerite destroys the innocent; protecting her makes August complicit. Her professional creed shatters. She burns nothing, decides nothing, and drinks alone in the bar where Rye holds court. POV August. Beat: the lowest point; identity as concierge collapses.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Rereading the diary, August deciphers its final page: an acrostic spelling her name, plus a time and place — the sealed ballroom, tonight, during the gala. Marguerite wrote as August to guarantee only August would keep reading. POV August. Beat: revelation reframing every prior clue; hope rekindled.

chapters.title: Gala Night
chapters.summary: During Rye's tribute, August slips upstairs and meets Marguerite alive, aged, unafraid. Marguerite explains the staged disappearance: Rye found her; hiding openly as staff was safer than running. But now he's here to finish it. POV Marguerite. Beat: reunion of the watcher and the watched; fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Sealed Ballroom
chapters.summary: Climax. Rye corners August and Marguerite in the ballroom, revealing he's known about the diary all along — Lund's inquiries flushed it out. Tomas and Sanna arrive; the staff form a wall. August triggers the hotel's ancient dictaphone system, broadcasting Rye's threats to the gala below. Beat: confrontation where attention itself becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: Confession in the Lobby
chapters.summary: With the whole hotel listening, Rye unravels — arrogance curdling into confession as guests, police, and press pour in. Marguerite steps out of the shadows and names him formally, twenty-two years late. POV August. Beat: catharsis; private witnessing made public at last.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Aftermath: Rye arrested; the 1998 case reopened. Marguerite must choose between protection and exposure and chooses to testify under her real name, reclaiming the identity she buried. August closes the file — the first case she closes by opening a door instead of shutting one. POV Marguerite, then August. Beat: justice rejoined to law, on their terms.

chapters.title: Checkout
chapters.summary: Lund reconciles with the cyclist's family; Sanna retires with honor; Tomas — revealed as the cyclist's brother who stayed to guard Marguerite — finally appears in a photograph. August returns the diary to Marguerite, blank pages and all. POV August. Beat: tenderness after tension; debts acknowledged.

chapters.title: A Parish for the Letter
chapters.summary: Weeks later, August takes a new guest's impossible request at the front desk and smiles. On the fourth floor, now reopened, a small plaque honors those the hotel sheltered. August understands at last: she was never just a finder of things, but a keeper of them. POV August. Beat: quiet resolution; identity rebuilt around chosen responsibility.
